reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 discusses SFE and twinning in CrCoNi, not CoCrFeNiTi. E2 describes a different alloy (FeCoNiAlTi) and precipitate design, not SFE or SRO. E3 addresses grain boundary nucleation of twins in CoCrFeMnNi, not bulk SFE or SRO effects. No evidence is provided for the SFE of CoCrFeNiTi, the effect of SRO on SFE, or the deformation mechanism transition.
premises: CoCrFeNiTi solid solution has a high intrinsic stacking fault energy (SFE)
High SFE favors planar glide and suppresses twinning, limiting work hardening
Short-range chemical order (SRO) can be induced without phase separation
Lower SFE promotes twinning or complex dislocation interactions, increasing strength
